newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS-High-grades see feeding frenzy.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS-High-grades see feeding frenzy.

text.p: Bullish market sentiment finally translated into trading activity on Thursday, as investors in high-grade U.S. corporate bonds went on a feeding frenzy of buying, traders said.
"The herd is back on board," said one investment-grade corporate bond trader. "Everything is tightening and there are a lot of buyers out there today."

Among high-yield bonds, the fading fortunes of Grand Union Co GUCU.O bonds grabbed attention in an otherwise quiet day of trading. Traders reported prices among most junk bonds were unchanged to slightly lower following weakness in stocks.
Traders said a thin forward calendar of new issues coupled with recent stability in the Treasury and stock markets was fueling the bullishness in investment-grade bonds.
"Things really started getting better following the CSX and Norfolk Southern deals," said a trader, citing the over $6 billion in railroad debt placed in recent weeks.
"Having that much debt absorbed so easily by investors really shows this market has legs," he added.
Traders said lower-rated investment-grade bonds saw the most substantial gains on Thursday, as buyers searched for higher yields.
Spreads on 20-year Viacom Inc bonds tightened by up to 15 basis points while 30-year Tele-Communications Inc debt tightened by up to seven basis points this week, traders said.
In junk bonds, Grand Union's $595 million in outstanding 12 percent senior notes were quoted four points lower by the end of the day after the company announced worse-than-expected earnings results.

The deteriorating outlook for the supermarket company prompted Moody's Investors Service to cut its rating on Grand Union's senior unsecured notes to Caa from B3 and Standard & Poor's to cut its rating to CCC from B-minus on Thursday.
Junk bonds also represented the bulk of new issue action on Thursday.
Late in the day, BancAmerica Securities sold $150 million in 10-year Station Casinos Inc senior subordinated notes to yield 10 1/4 percent in a 144a private placement.
BancAmerica was forced to postpone the offering in April due to poor market conditions after committing to buy the entire issue from the company.
The offering priced within the original price talk range of 10 1/8 percent to 10 1/4 percent. A BancAmerica official said around 30 investors participated in the offering.
ITC Deltcom Inc priced $200 million in 10-year senior notes, rated B3/B, to yield 11 percent in a blowout 144a private placement offering by Morgan Stanley & Co.
The deal, which was substantially oversubscribed, priced on the inside of price talk and was increased in size by $25 million, sources close to the deal said.
The notes, priced at par, were heard trading at 102 3/4 toward the end of the day.
ITC provides local telephone service in the Southern U.S.
Among investment-grade new issues, Susa Partnership (Storage USA) sold $100 million in 20-year notes, rated Baa3/BBB-minus, to yield 8.20 percent via Goldman Sachs & Co.
In the broader markets, the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 27.05 to close at 7330.18.
U.S. Treasuries closed higher, boosted by overseas buying and a better-than-expected Treasury auction.
The price of the 30-year benchmark Treasury rose 20/32 to 95.19, pushing the yield down to 6.98 percent.
